private_notes.observations: No prior panel rates or allocations are available. Our fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start at a moderate margin, then use published panel rates and observed allocated hours to assess price sensitivity and adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $350 rate was $76 above both competitors’ $274 rates, yet we received 190 hours and approximately $28,538 in profit. The effect of a rate change on our allocation remains uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Lower our rate moderately to test whether a more competitive price increases allocated hours enough to improve profit. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: Lowering our rate from $350 in Q1 to $315 in Q2 increased allocated hours from 190 to 349 and profit from $28,538 to $40,184. Both other firms held their rates at $274.
private_notes.plan: Test a further modest reduction to $300. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q2 before making another adjustment; avoid a large cut that could sacrifice too much margin.

private_notes.observations: With competitors holding at $274, lowering our rate from $350 to $315 to $300 increased quarterly profit from $28,538 to $40,184 to $44,450. The added hours have more than offset the reduced margin so far.
private_notes.plan: Test $285, a modest reduction toward the estimated profit-maximizing rate. Compare the resulting profit and allocation with Q3 before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: Reducing our rate from $350 to $285 increased quarterly profit from $28,538 to $47,322 while competitors held at $274. Profit has risen with each reduction so far.
private_notes.plan: Test $270, just below the competitors' published rates. Compare the additional hours and profit with Q4 before deciding whether to reduce further.

private_notes.observations: Competitors held at $274 throughout Q1–Q5. Lowering our rate increased both hours and quarterly profit, but the profit gain from $285 to $270 was only $615, suggesting we are near the optimum.
private_notes.plan: Set $273 to test a slightly higher margin while remaining below both competitors. Compare Q6 profit and hours with Q5 before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: Both competitors have held at $274 throughout. Profit rose from approximately $47,950 at $270 in Q5 to $48,038 at $273 in Q6, despite fewer allocated hours. The observed results suggest $273 is near the profit-maximizing rate.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $273. Reassess if competitors change rates or the allocation pattern shifts.

private_notes.observations: Competitors have held at $274 throughout. Our $273 rate yielded 658 hours and about $48,038 profit in each of the last two quarters, exceeding the observed profits at other tested rates.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $273 while competitor rates and allocations remain stable; reassess if either changes.
